datasets: Violent Crime Rate per 1,000 Residents - Community Statistical Area (BNIA Vital Signs via Open Baltimore; data/crime.csv, column viol23)
Percent of Households Living Below the Poverty Line - Community Statistical Area (BNIA Vital Signs via Open Baltimore, ACS-derived; data/poverty.csv, column hhpov23)
build_error: Builds only because GOTOOLCHAIN=auto downloaded go1.27.2 (go.mod: go 1.27.2). With GOTOOLCHAIN=local: 'go: go.mod requires go >= 1.27.2 (running go 1.24.0; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)'. go vet: analysis.go:87:4: fmt.Print call has possible Printf formatting directive %s
concurrency_primitives: 2 goroutines load the two CSVs and send Result on a buffered channel (main.go:4-6, concurrent.go); 3-goroutine worker pool with jobs/results channels (cap 55) and sync.WaitGroup parses two floats per community (workers.go:11-33); all analysis sequential
design_patterns: README claims Strategy (RankingStrategy/CrimeStrategy/PovertyStrategy) but no such code exists; actual structure is a flat procedural split across 6 files with a worker-pool helper
questions: Which Baltimore community has the highest violent crime rate?
Which Baltimore community has the highest household poverty percentage?
What are the average violent crime rate and household poverty percentage across communities?
Which communities have both violent crime and poverty above their averages?
Which communities have violent crime above average but poverty below average?
overview: Short procedural Go split across six files (load, join, workers, analysis, visualization). Data is parsed into typed structs by a worker pool and then converted back to strings so each of five analysis functions can re-parse it; the README describes a Strategy pattern that is not in the code. No tests, a go vet failure, typos and inconsistent formatting; reads as a first draft.
stakeholder_value: No stakeholders are named. Q1-Q3 are single-dataset maxima and averages; Q4/Q5 (above-average crime vs above/below-average poverty) are the only cross-dataset questions and Q5's high-crime/low-poverty flag has some planning value, but Q4's output is garbled by a Printf bug and everything is threshold counting on 55 pre-aggregated rows.
issues: go.mod requires go 1.27.2; builds only via undocumented automatic toolchain download, fails with GOTOOLCHAIN=local
go vet fails: analysis.go:87 fmt.Print with format directives; RQ4 output prints literal '%s | Crime: %.2f ...' strings
README claims a Strategy pattern (RankingStrategy/CrimeStrategy/PovertyStrategy) that does not exist in the code
Ships a Windows .exe, not a macOS build
Token concurrency: 3-worker pool parses 110 floats, analyses sequential, results converted back to strings
Datasets are pre-aggregated 55-row BNIA indicator tables, not raw records; one column used from each
Nondeterministic output order and detail lines printed before their question headers
rationale: Credit for two real, bundled Open Baltimore CSA tables that join cleanly and for a program that executes. Points lost across the board because the build depends on an undocumented toolchain download and fails vet, the concurrency and memory requirements are met only nominally, the README's design pattern is absent from the code, there are no tests, and the vet bug corrupts one of the five answers at runtime. Total 46, F; lateness flagged but not deducted.
